newsitem.title: USA: Florida man admits cash-for-prizes postal scheme.
newsitem.headline: Florida man admits cash-for-prizes postal scheme.

text.p: A Florida man has pleaded guilty for his role in a national multi-million dollar mail solicitation scheme in which postal patrons were told they had won big prizes but had to send in money to collect their gifts, court officials said Monday.
Eric Weitz, 27, of Boca Raton, pleaded guilty Friday in Manhattan federal court to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and evasion of taxes on cash proceeds of the scheme, they said.

As part of his guilty plea he agreed to forfeit his residence, banking and brokerage accounts and other property estimated to be worth more than $1.5 million. He also faces a possible maximum prison term of 10 years and fines of $500,000.

Federal prosecutors said Weitz and others were involved in the two-year scheme in which they sent letters telling recipients they had won cash and other prizes that were never awarded and directing them to send money in order to collect their prizes. The solicitations were sent on the letterheads of bogus companies with different names including "First National Services," "Merchandise Control Services" and "Capital Sweeps Reserve."

Prosecutors said postal patrons sent millions of dollars to these companies. The money was collected by East Coast Data Entry Systems of Valley Cottage, N.Y., a corporation controlled by Weitz and others.
Two other defendants have previously pleaded guilty for their roles in the scheme.
